result:
I can't make a valid case for 144/35. Under the problem's rules, the bound below rules it out.

Every removal except possibly a final one is triggered by a double, and each double is used once. So N equals the number of pair-removals plus at most one extra removal for leftover cards with no double. Debater B's sum, Σ⌊L/2⌋ over the runs, gives the pair-removals. I rechecked their values (f(2)=3/11, f(3)=3/55, f(4)=1/165) and the total 138/55 holds. That means:

E[N] ≤ 138/55 + 1 = 193/55 ≈ 3.51 < 144/35 ≈ 4.11.

So 144/35 cannot be correct on any reading where the leftover step adds at most one removal. The solution also shows no intermediate values, so its claimed result is unsupported.

Debater B's 138/55 is not exact either. It is a lower bound, since it omits the leftover term. The true answer lies in [138/55, 193/55]. Pinning it down requires computing the leftover probability or running a Monte Carlo simulation, which I have not done.
